description:
Elixir: `def f("--" <> rest)` and `case s do "--" <> rest -> ... end` match a binary starting with the literal prefix and bind the remainder. fz at d0c490721: in a function head it fails with `error[internal/post-resolution-leftover]: quoted function decode failed: unsupported quoted pattern head `<>`` (src/compiler2/quoted_function.rs:575, at <generated>); in a case it fails with `quoted function decode failed: invalid any value ref: ExpectedTag`. Both are internal errors, not refusals. The byte spelling `<<45, 45, rest::binary>>` works. Expected: `<>` with a literal binary left side is a pattern on every path (head, case, receive, fn, `=`), meaning what the equivalent bitstring pattern means; a non-literal left side is refused as Elixir refuses it. Blocks fz-sc8.16, whose OptionParser is written the way Elixir writes it.

## UNBLOCKS

- ○ fz-sc8.16 P2 OptionParser.parse/2 with strict:

Approved page /Users/j5n/Workspace/fz-sc8.56.html. Folded in, by agreement: a pinned unsized binary segment <<^p::binary, r::binary>> is sized by its value (it silently never matches today), so ^p <> rest works; and a literal list ++ rest in a pattern is the list pattern it stands for. The decoder recognises the expander's sugared call by a stamped meta key (as __fz_from_brackets__), never by the Kernel alias. The receive form is covered by fz-sc8.60.
title: A "prefix" <> rest pattern matches a binary that starts with prefix
